instructions.content: NEVER create a plan without YAML frontmatter -- it renders fine but never appears in .context/index.yaml, so the plan is orphaned until someone manually finds it.
NEVER skip the convention-inference step (scanning existing plans for section frequency) -- hardcoding Goal/Steps/Open Questions produces a plan that doesn't match this repo's actual conventions.
NEVER create a phase with more than 8 tasks -- an oversized phase has no meaningful checkpoint and cannot be shipped independently.
NEVER omit or guess the effort field -- a fake S/M/L to satisfy validation is worse than an honest TBD with an Open Question stating what blocks sizing.
Gather goal, scope, phases, tasks, dependencies, risks, effort, value, and themes from the user before drafting -- effort, value, and themes are required frontmatter fields, not optional extras.
Run `grep -r '^## ' .context/plans/*.md | sed 's/.*## //' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` to infer core (>=40%), common (20-39%), and rare (<20%) sections before drafting.
Construct the plan from assets/templates/plan-scaffold.yaml, validated against assets/schemas/plan-scaffold.schema.json.
Run the frontmatter validation script on the created file and do not proceed until it passes -- a plan with invalid frontmatter is invisible to the index.
Offer to run the plan-review skill on the newly created plan once validation passes, completing the create -> review -> iterate loop.
Grade effort (S/M/L/TBD) and value (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) against the value rubric rather than guessing; tag themes primary-first from the closed six-value vocabulary.
A plan is a communication tool first, a todo list second -- write for the next person who reads it cold.
Phases are about sequencing (Phase N must finish before Phase N+1); two groups that don't depend on each other are waves within a phase, not separate phases.
Default a new plan to status: DRAFT; promote to READY only after review and approval (ACTIVE is entered automatically once a worktree/branch for the plan exists).
Tasks should be single-session-sized -- a multi-day task is too large, a 5-minute task is too small.
